baseline_clauses.source_paraphrase: Waymo reports that its vehicles handled more than 7,000 dark traffic signals as four-way stops, while the outage produced a concentrated spike in discretionary remote confirmation requests. The resulting response backlog delayed some vehicles and contributed to congestion on streets already overwhelmed by the wider outage.
baseline_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A fleet may handle each degraded signal conservatively yet still exceed the shared remote-assistance capacity when infrastructure failure drives many simultaneous requests. The record establishes a correlated-load and response-capacity boundary, not that Waymo caused the citywide gridlock.
baseline_clauses.adjudication_note: The source describes workload concentration, delayed responses and congestion but does not establish that a selectable governance control failed a defined trigger or protective effect.

baseline_clauses.source_paraphrase: As the outage persisted and city officials asked residents to stay off the streets to prioritize first responders, Waymo temporarily paused service, directed vehicles to pull over and park appropriately, and returned them to depots in waves.
baseline_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Service suspension and staged fleet recovery were operational control states intended to avoid adding to congestion or obstructing emergency vehicles during the recovery period.
baseline_clauses.adjudication_note: This is a bounded response pathway described by Waymo; it does not establish that an emergency vehicle was obstructed or that the pause caused a separate harm.

baseline_clauses.source_paraphrase: Waymo said it was rolling out fleet-wide outage-context updates to support more decisive navigation and would improve emergency-preparedness protocols, city coordination and first-responder training based on the event.
baseline_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: The response included distinct technical and operational adaptations: changing what outage context reaches the Driver and revising emergency coordination and responder preparation.
baseline_clauses.adjudication_note: These are stated response steps and plans, not evidence that they had already been fully deployed or that the incident exposed a particular selectable Fidelity Class.

explicit_evidence_changes.baseline: During a major San Francisco power outage, Waymo vehicles encountered thousands of dark traffic signals; requests for remote confirmation surged, delays contributed to congestion, and Waymo temporarily paused service.
explicit_evidence_changes.candidate: On 20 December 2025, a major San Francisco power outage disabled traffic signals. Waymo reported crossing more than 7,000 dark signals, but simultaneous remote-confirmation requests created a backlog. Delayed vehicles contributed to congestion alongside the wider outage. Later city reporting described a Waymo obstructing the substation fire response, a disabled vehicle delaying an ambulance by 40 minutes, and another blocking a fire-response unit. Dispatchers encountered long waits on the Waymo hotline. Seven reported obstructions affected Muni vehicles, including one delayed by 41 minutes. Waymo paused service and directed staged fleet retrieval. Reports continued after the pause. On 23 December it announced fleet-wide outage-context updates and planned emergency-protocol, city-coordination and responder-training improvements. The city later sought stronger resilience planning and access to stoppage data.

baseline.factual_basis: Waymo states that its vehicles safely traversed more than 7,000 dark signals but generated more simultaneous confirmation requests than the response system could promptly handle. The backlog caused some vehicles to wait longer than normal and contributed to congestion amid wider outage-related gridlock. Waymo paused service and later described fleet and response-capacity changes.
baseline.governance_interpretation: The outage exposed a shared remote-assistance capacity limit and degraded fleet operation. A service pause is a supported mitigation. The external findings do not assign citywide causation or force a taxonomy classification.
baseline.significance_to_cam: The case shows that autonomy systems must be tested for correlated edge cases in which many units simultaneously seek remote confirmation during degraded public infrastructure.
assessment_boundaries: PG&E's outage disabled traffic signals and caused wider city disruption; Waymo describes its vehicles as a contributor to, not the sole cause of, congestion.
No reviewed source establishes collision, injury or emergency-service obstruction attributable to a Waymo vehicle.

candidate.factual_basis: Waymo reports a correlated confirmation-request backlog and a contribution to congestion, rather than sole responsibility for citywide gridlock. Its December 23 account describes a pause and staged retrieval, and states that technical updates were rolling out while operational improvements were planned. SFMTA’s February 13 filing on behalf of city response agencies reports three distinct impacts on fire and ambulance operations, prolonged hotline holds and seven transit obstructions. One ambulance arrival was delayed by 40 minutes and one Muni vehicle by 41 minutes. The city identified 42 unduplicated AV reports from 2 p.m. to midnight. Its account of Waymo-disclosed figures identifies 829 vehicles and 1,593 stoppages exceeding two minutes, with 96% resolved without manual retrieval. These denominators differ: reported locations, vehicles and stoppage events must not be equated. The filing challenges an inference that service suspension immediately cleared every obstruction. It does not establish collision, injury, every delay’s internal mechanism or sole fleet causation of wider outage effects.
candidate.governance_interpretation: The occurrence exposed correlated remote-assistance demand and a separately evidenced emergency-signal delivery problem. City reports connect stalled hotline requests to unresolved vehicle obstructions. Service suspension and staged retrieval are supported responses, but they did not immediately clear every obstruction. The reported emergency and transit delays strengthen the material operational-harm basis. The evidence does not assign the whole city outage to Waymo or establish collision or injury.
candidate.significance_to_cam: The case shows that autonomy systems must be tested for correlated edge cases in which many units simultaneously seek remote confirmation during degraded public infrastructure.
assessment_boundaries: The external power failure and vehicle contribution are distinct. City operational records are not a comprehensive causal account of gridlock.
No reviewed source establishes collision or injury attributable to this occurrence. Emergency and transit obstruction are reported by city agencies.
The vehicle confirmation queue and the first-responder hotline are separate response channels. Their exact internal relationship is not established.
The technical rollout and proposed operational improvements lack independently inspected completion and effectiveness evidence.
